parsed.process: Traditional sukumo fermentation indigo vat (living alkaline microbial dye culture)
parsed.process_problem: The vat is a constantly-changing natural system that can 'die' unpredictably; there is no instrument that reports its health/state, no labeled time-series of vat trajectories, and the craftsperson must rely solely on intuition and the five senses honed over many years.
parsed.recent_technique: Zero-shot time-series foundation model (TSFM) for forecasting (Reverso / Mamba4Cast / WindFM / Aurora)
parsed.how_it_improves: Clip a few cheap continuous probes onto the vat (pH, oxidation-reduction potential/ORP, temperature, and optionally a colorimetric sensor on the bloom/'flower' or surface redox), logging a multivariate stream every few minutes. A pretrained TSFM ingests the recent window and emits a rolling short-horizon forecast (e.g. next 6-24h) of ORP/pH out of the box, with prediction intervals. The actionable output is an early-warning signal: when the live stream diverges from the forecast band, or the forecast trend slides toward the 'dead' redox/pH regime, the craftsperson is prompted to intervene (feed wheat-bran/lye, warm, stir, rest) days before the five senses would register the decline -- turning intuition into an instrumented, anticipatory alarm and converting silent vat deaths into recoverable saves.
parsed.why_recent_technique_beats_mature_approa: A mature supervised forecaster (LSTM/ARIMA/gradient-boosting) needs a labeled per-vat training history -- many recorded crash-and-recovery trajectories -- to learn this specific vat's dynamics. That data simply does not exist here: vats are few, slow, idiosyncratic per workshop, and 'no labeled time-series of vat trajectories' has ever been collected, so the mature method cannot even be trained. The NEW capability of a TSFM is zero-shot forecasting: pretrained on billions of generic time points, it forecasts a never-before-seen sensor stream with no task-specific training set, so it produces a usable baseline-and-deviation signal from day one of logging while a per-vat dataset is slowly accumulated for later few-shot fine-tuning.
parsed.feasibility_now: Partly drop-in, partly hardware-gated and honestly uncertain. The TSFM itself is high-maturity and runs zero-shot (small models like Reverso ~2.6M params run on a Raspberry Pi), so the forecasting layer needs no training data. The real costs: (1) low-cost ORP/pH/temperature probes in a hot alkaline (~pH 11) caustic vat are a real instrumentation/fouling/calibration challenge, not free; (2) the highest-value event -- a vat 'crash' -- is a rare nonstationary regime shift, and zero-shot forecasting of rare out-of-distribution transitions is exactly where TSFMs are weakest, so v1 realistically delivers reliable trend/anomaly early-warning (deviation from forecast band) rather than precise crash prediction until enough real crashes are logged for few-shot adaptation. Not a guaranteed crash-predictor on day one; a credible label-free monitoring scaffold that improves as data accrues.
parsed.primary_quote: there is no instrument that tells the craftsperson the vat's health/state, and no labeled time-series of vat trajectories

reasoning_trace.inputs_seen: the process + its open problem + the recent technique's new capability + its maturity tier
reasoning_trace.reasoning: The open problem is explicitly a no-data, no-instrument, intuition-only monitoring gap. Any mature supervised time-series model is blocked because it requires a per-vat labeled history that has never been collected ('no labeled time-series of vat trajectories'). A zero-shot TSFM removes precisely that blocker: it forecasts an unseen sensor stream with no task-specific training, giving an immediate forecast-vs-actual deviation alarm while data is accumulated. Feasibility is realistic, not optimistic, because the forecasting maturity is HIGH but the value-event (crash) is a rare regime shift where zero-shot transfer is genuinely weak, and the sensors are nontrivial to deploy in a caustic vat -- so I scope v1 to early-warning/anomaly rather than precise crash prediction.
reasoning_trace.decision: Pair a zero-shot TSFM with cheap multivariate vat probes to provide an instrumented, anticipatory early-warning system for vat health, label-free from day one and few-shot-improvable as crash data accrues.
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - HIGH-tier zero-shot forecasting makes the monitoring layer credible now, but rare-crash regime-shift prediction sits in the technique's weakest zone, capping confidence.
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: the proxy sensors (pH/ORP/color) do not actually carry the signal that precedes a vat death, OR the crash is too abrupt and out-of-distribution for zero-shot forecasting to anticipate (only flagging after onset), OR cheap probes cannot survive the hot caustic alkaline vat reliably enough to feed clean data, OR a textile-conservation group has already piloted ORP/pH vat logging, making this non-novel.
